intro: Medium dogs, roughly 25 to 60 pounds, are big enough for hiking and rough play with older kids yet small enough for most cars, rentals and apartments with weight limits. Size within this range matters less than energy, though. A working breed of the same weight as a spaniel may need twice the exercise and far more mental work. Look next at grooming, since several of these coats need regular trims, and at barking if you have close neighbors.

picks.description: The Australian Cattle Dog, about 35 to 50 pounds, is tough, intelligent and loyal, with a short coat that needs little grooming beyond weekly brushing, though it sheds moderately and drops undercoat seasonally. It ranks last for general households for three reasons in our breed data: energy is high, training is rated hard because it is independent and tests boundaries, and it is not considered good with cats. Cattle Dogs need hours of activity and a job, and they may nip at heels when herding instinct takes over, which matters around small children despite being rated fine with kids. They are protective and can be wary of strangers. For an experienced owner on a farm or with a serious outdoor routine, they are superb partners.
picks.best_for: Experienced owners with land or a demanding outdoor routine
picks.quirky_fact: Australian Cattle Dog puppies are born white and develop their blue or red speckled coat as they grow.
picks.skip_if: You have cats, are a first-time owner, or can't provide hours of daily work

picks.description: The Beagle is a 20 to 30 pound scent hound with a short coat that needs only weekly brushing, and it is friendly and good with children, cats and other dogs. Two things push it near the bottom for general households. First, barking is rated high: Beagles bay and howl, especially when bored or left alone, which can upset neighbors. Second, training is moderate at best because the nose wins over commands, so recall off lead is unreliable and a securely fenced yard is needed. Energy is high, so plan on an hour or more of walking with plenty of sniffing time. They shed moderately and love food, so portion control matters. In a house with a yard and someone home, they are cheerful companions.
picks.best_for: Houses with yards wanting a cheerful, low-grooming family hound
picks.quirky_fact: A Beagle's long ears help sweep scent toward its nose as it tracks along the ground.
picks.skip_if: You live in an apartment, share walls or need reliable off-lead recall

picks.description: The Australian Shepherd, about 40 to 65 pounds, is one of the most capable and trainable breeds on this list, and it is good with children, cats and other dogs. It ranks lower because its energy is very high: most Aussies need well over an hour of vigorous daily exercise plus a job such as agility, herding or advanced training. Without that, they invent their own work, including herding children, chewing and barking. The medium double coat sheds moderately all year and heavily in season, so weekly brushing becomes several sessions a week at those times. Aussies can be wary of strangers and need early socialization. They are excellent for experienced, active owners and too much dog for a casual household.
picks.best_for: Experienced, very active owners who want a dog-sports partner
picks.quirky_fact: Despite the name, the Australian Shepherd was developed mainly on ranches in the western United States.
picks.skip_if: You can't provide vigorous exercise and a daily mental job

picks.description: The Toller is the smallest retriever, about 35 to 50 pounds, with a red, water-resistant double coat. It is easy to train, alert and good with children, cats and other dogs. Energy is high and it needs both physical and mental work: an hour or more daily of retrieving, swimming or dog sports. Tollers are known for a high-pitched scream when excited, which can be a problem in shared buildings, though the breed's overall barking rating is moderate. The coat sheds moderately, with heavier seasonal sheds, and needs weekly brushing and more during those periods. They can be reserved with strangers. For active households that want a retriever's trainability in a smaller frame, the Toller is a strong pick.
picks.best_for: Active owners wanting a compact, trainable retriever for dog sports
picks.quirky_fact: Tollers lure ducks closer by playing along the shoreline, a hunting technique called tolling.
picks.skip_if: You share walls and an excitable, high-pitched voice would cause friction

picks.description: The Brittany is a lean 30 to 40 pound bird dog that is easy to train and friendly with children, cats and other dogs. Its energy is high, closer to a working dog than a pet spaniel: expect to provide 60 to 90 minutes of running, hiking or field games every day. In return, the short, medium-length coat is easy to keep, needing only a weekly brush, though it does shed moderately. Brittanys are sensitive and respond to gentle, consistent training, and they can be soft-tempered if handled harshly. Barking is moderate. They suit runners, hikers and families with a large yard far better than people expecting a relaxed indoor dog, and they can become anxious and destructive without enough outlet.
picks.best_for: Runners and hikers wanting a trainable, low-grooming bird dog
picks.quirky_fact: Brittanys are often born with naturally short or no tails, a trait that runs in the breed.
picks.skip_if: Your household is mostly indoors or exercise time is limited

picks.description: The English Springer Spaniel, around 40 to 50 pounds, is easy to train, friendly and good with children, cats and other dogs, which is why it is a long-standing family favorite. It ranks below the first four only because energy is high: plan on 60 to 90 minutes of daily exercise, including off-lead running or retrieving in a safe area, plus some training to occupy its mind. Under-exercised Springers can become restless and noisy indoors. The medium, wavy coat sheds moderately and needs brushing a couple of times a week and trimming around the ears and feet. Those long ears also need weekly cleaning. Springers are affectionate and want to be with their people, so they handle long hours alone poorly.
picks.best_for: Active families wanting an affectionate, easy-to-train outdoor companion
picks.quirky_fact: The name comes from the breed's original job of springing, or flushing, game birds from cover for hunters.
picks.skip_if: You can't give 60 to 90 minutes of exercise or the dog will often be alone

picks.description: The American Water Spaniel is a 25 to 45 pound hunting dog with a curly, water-resistant coat and medium energy. An hour of daily activity, ideally including swimming or retrieving, keeps it content. It is friendly, loyal and good with children, cats and other dogs, and it bonds closely with its family. Training is moderate: willing, but it can be sensitive and sometimes reserved with strangers, so early socialization helps. The coat sheds moderately and needs weekly brushing to prevent tangles, plus a good dry after swims to avoid a damp-dog smell. Barking is moderate, usually as an alert. Lifespan is a little shorter than some others here, about 10 to 12 years. It suits outdoorsy families near water who want a compact retriever.
picks.best_for: Outdoorsy families near water wanting a compact, loyal retriever
picks.quirky_fact: The American Water Spaniel is the state dog of Wisconsin, where it was developed to retrieve from small boats.
picks.skip_if: You want a dog that stays dry and clean on outings

picks.description: The Field Spaniel is a quieter, less common relative of the Cocker and Springer, weighing about 35 to 50 pounds. Energy is medium, so a daily hour of walking, fetch or swimming is usually enough, and it tends to be calm indoors once exercised. It is gentle, friendly and good with children, cats and other dogs, which makes it an easy household dog. Training is moderate; Field Spaniels are sensitive and respond best to calm, reward-based methods rather than harsh corrections. The medium, wavy coat sheds moderately and needs brushing once or twice a week plus trimming around the ears and feet. Long ears need regular checks for infection. Because the breed is rare, expect to wait for a puppy from a reputable breeder.
picks.best_for: Families wanting a gentle, mid-energy spaniel that is calm indoors
picks.quirky_fact: Field Spaniels came close to disappearing in the mid-twentieth century before breeders rebuilt the population.
picks.skip_if: You need a puppy soon or prefer firm, quick training

picks.description: The Lagotto Romagnolo is a 24 to 35 pound Italian water dog with medium energy, a dense curly coat that sheds little, and a long lifespan of 14 to 16 years. A long daily walk plus a sniffing game or short training session meets its needs. Lagottos are affectionate and good with children, cats and other dogs. The coat is the main commitment: brush to the skin every week or two to stop mats and plan a full trim a few times a year. Training is moderate; Lagottos are clever but easily distracted by scents, and a bored one may dig. Barking is moderate. It is a good fit for owners who want a sociable, mid-energy dog and don't mind regular grooming appointments.
picks.best_for: Owners wanting a low-shedding, affectionate dog with manageable energy
picks.quirky_fact: Lagottos are the traditional truffle-hunting dogs of Italy and are still used for that work.
picks.skip_if: You want a wash-and-go coat or a perfect lawn

picks.description: The Standard Schnauzer, about 30 to 50 pounds, earns the top spot because it combines medium energy, easy training and a low-shedding coat. A brisk daily walk of 45 to 60 minutes plus a training session or puzzle toy keeps it settled, and it learns house rules quickly. It is good with children, cats and other dogs, especially when raised with them, and it often lives 13 to 16 years. The wiry coat sheds lightly but needs weekly brushing, a beard wipe after meals, and clipping or hand-stripping every few months. The main trade-off is watchfulness: Schnauzers bark at strangers and unusual sounds, which makes them good alarms but means teaching a quiet cue early, especially in attached housing.
picks.best_for: Families wanting a trainable, low-shedding medium dog with moderate energy
picks.quirky_fact: The Standard Schnauzer is the original Schnauzer size, and the Miniature and Giant Schnauzers were developed from it.
picks.skip_if: You want a silent dog or can't keep up with coat trims

faqs.question: What size counts as a medium dog?
faqs.answer: Most people mean dogs of roughly 25 to 60 pounds and about 17 to 23 inches at the shoulder, though breed clubs and landlords draw the line differently. Check your lease or building rules for the exact weight limit, and remember that a puppy's adult weight is only an estimate, so look at both parents if you can.

faqs.question: Which medium dog is the calmest?
faqs.answer: On this list, the Standard Schnauzer, Lagotto Romagnolo, Field Spaniel and American Water Spaniel are rated medium rather than high for energy. They still need a solid daily walk and some play or training, but they settle more easily indoors than the Australian Shepherd, Brittany, Toller or Australian Cattle Dog, which are bred for long working days.

faqs.question: Which medium dogs shed the least?
faqs.answer: The Standard Schnauzer and Lagotto Romagnolo are the two low-shedding breeds here. The Schnauzer has a wiry coat that needs clipping or hand-stripping a few times a year, and the Lagotto has dense curls that need regular trims. No dog is allergen-free, but less loose hair makes cleaning easier. The rest of the list sheds at a moderate level.

faqs.question: Are medium dogs good for apartments?
faqs.answer: Some are, if the building allows their weight. Moderate-energy breeds that are not big barkers, such as the Field Spaniel or Lagotto, adjust well with daily walks. High-energy herders like the Australian Shepherd and Australian Cattle Dog, and the vocal Beagle, are harder in shared buildings because boredom and noise show up quickly.

faqs.question: Which medium dogs are good with cats?
faqs.answer: According to our breed data, every breed on this list except the Australian Cattle Dog is generally good with cats. Individual dogs still vary, so introduce them slowly and supervise early meetings. Hunting breeds such as the Beagle, Brittany and spaniels may chase cats outdoors even when they accept the family cat inside.

seo_title: Best Medium Dog Breeds for Families (2026 Guide)
answer: The Standard Schnauzer, Lagotto Romagnolo and Field Spaniel lead this list of medium dogs because they combine moderate energy with good manners around children, cats and other dogs. The deciding factor for most households is daily exercise, so match the breed's energy to the time you really have.
method: We filtered a 150-breed dataset for medium-sized breeds, then ordered them by energy level, trainability, compatibility with children, cats and other dogs, and barking, putting the easiest all-round household fits first.
